author: Adam Aucoin Staff Writer
title: Woodstock girls hold off Springfield | Local | rutlandherald.com
text:
SPRINGFIELD — One play can energize a team and swing the momentum of a game.
In the Woodstock girls soccer team's 3-1 win against Springfield, it looked like the Wasps might put a final dagger into the Cosmos midway through the second half, already up 2-0.
The Wasps had an opportunity with Cosmos goalie Tate Simoneau out of goal and the ball sitting close to lip of the goal.
It was anybody's ball to finish it off and put Springfield to bed, but it was Cosmos sophomore Taylor Tomberg getting to it to clear it away and give Springfield life.
That play seemed to give the Cosmos the spark they needed to push hard for a goal to cut into the lead.
With 14:05 to play, the hard-kicking Harper Palmer rocketed one toward the right side of the goal that went just wide with Woodstock keeper Jess Baumann getting her finger tips on it.
The pressure just kept on coming. Tomberg, who was moved up to the offensive end late in the contest, had a shot that went just high off a corner kick by Ava Johnson.
Springfield's relentless attack finally paid off with 8:57 to play when Palmer fed a pass into the box as Tomberg had a perfectly timed run to run on and put a shot past Baumann to pull the Cosmos within one.
The Cosmos kept pushing to find the equalizer, but it wouldn't come. Woodstock junior Julia Barry quelled Springfield's run, scoring with 2:43 to play to effectively put the game away.
"They just didn't want to lose. It's a young team, so it's a confidence thing," said Springfield coach Ray Curren. "This is probably the best team we've played in four games, so it shook them a bit in the first half.
"We have some guts and they have a lot of things to build on."
Woodstock is a very experienced club, but there are a bunch of players that are taking on bigger roles this year, so dealing with the pressure of maintaining a lead was something they could learn from.
"We have to lean on our most experienced players to maintain composure when the game gets unwieldy," said Woodstock coach Greg LaBella.
"That's something that's going to happen with maturity. There's 13 returning varsity players. Half of them were key players last year and the other half are really in their first intense varsity matches. A Woodstock-Springfield match is always intense going back for years and years and years."
Tomberg's goal was the first of her varsity career. She adds another wrinkle to a balanced Springfield attack that has had six different girls score through four games.
"She's certainly our fastest player and she's a returning starter from last year," Curren said. "We'd like to play her more up, but we can't play her in two places at once.
"We took some chances at the end and they got the third goal, so it is what it is."
Woodstock buried its first goal with 27:34 left in the first half. Sadie Boulbol, who was a threat all game long for the Wasps on the attack, dished it off to junior Ava Rich in the right side of the box and Rich scored.
Hannah Lantiegne pushed Woodstock's lead to two with 6:19 to play.
Soon after the Lantiegne goal, Springfield had its best opportunity of the opening half with a well-struck shot to the left side of the goal, but Baumann dove to turn it away and force the Cosmos to take a corner kick.
Both keepers had busy days. Baumann made 13 saves with nine of them coming after the break. Simoneau had 12 saves for Springfield.
Springfield (2-1-1) has another tough test on Saturday, hosting Division I Brattleboro. Woodstock (2-1) is at Hartford on Tuesday.
